articles.headline: Labour council packs half-term with free and low-cost family fun
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council is giving families a half-term full of free and low-cost things to do, from Spooks in the City and pumpkin trails to science shows, library crafts and sports camps.
body: Swansea's Labour council is making sure families have plenty of free and low-cost ways to keep children entertained this half-term, with spooky events, creative workshops, science shows and sports activities across the city.

Labour's Cabinet Member for Development, Cllr Andrew Williams, said: "There is so much to enjoy in Swansea this half-term, with a packed programme of activities taking place right across the destination."

The week builds up to the free Spooks in the City event at St David's Place on 31 October, from 1pm to 6pm. This year's Día de los Muertos theme brings traditional music, dance performances, face painting, craft workshops, circus acts and mariachi bands to the city centre.

Until 1 November, Swansea Museum is hosting pumpkin-themed activities, including a free trail and activity pack. A Tricksy Pumpkin Workshop on 29 October, from 10am to 1pm, lets children create a mischievous pumpkin trick to surprise friends and family. The Spooky Halloween Land Train runs along Swansea Promenade from 26 to 31 October, with six daily departures from 2.30pm. Every child receives a free "I Survived the Halloween Ghost Land Train 2026" souvenir certificate, and advance booking is essential.

At the Glynn Vivian, families can explore the latest exhibitions and join free workshops, including a cardboard memory houses workshop on 28 October, where participants build a 3D house from recycled materials and personal photographs. Booking is required. The Swansea Science Festival returns on 30 and 31 October with science shows, interactive workshops and hands-on activities, plus a special session with The Traitors stars Fiona and Amanda and Swansea University psychologist Dr Alex Jones on deception, trust and human behaviour.

Swansea's 17 libraries are hosting family activities throughout the week, including Splat the Pumpkin with local author Chrissie Lackey and a Make a Book Flower craft session. At Penlan Leisure Centre, the Sport & Health team is running the Us Girls Camp on 27 October and the Street Games Camp on 28 October, both from 10am to 3pm.

The Dylan Thomas Centre rounds off the week. On 30 October, children can make their own quill from naturally shed feathers in Autumnal Spells: Quivering Quills, and on 31 October the free Autumnal Spell Generator offers puppets, fancy dress, poetry activities, storytelling games and a sensory corner.

Labour councillors know that school holidays can be expensive for families. By keeping so much of this programme free or low-cost, and spreading it across museums, galleries, libraries and leisure centres, the Labour administration is making sure every family in Swansea can join in.
This half-term programme shows Labour's priorities for Swansea: supporting families, backing the city's cultural venues and giving children great things to do close to home.

images.alt: A land train decorated with skeletons, a witch figure and black drapes, lit up at dusk on Swansea Promenade
Two costumed mascots, one dressed as Frankenstein's monster, pose at a Spooks in the City event

articles.sourceTitle: Top things to do in Swansea this half-term

articles.headline: Labour council helps older residents check if they can claim Pension Credit
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council is running a free Pension Credit drop-in at Ty Dewi Sant in Fforestfach on 28 October, where its Financial Inclusion Team will check what older residents can claim.
body: Swansea's Labour council is helping older residents find out whether they are entitled to Pension Credit, with a free drop-in session at Ty Dewi Sant in Fforestfach on 28 October.
Anyone over State Pension age may be eligible to make a claim. The council's Financial Inclusion Team will be on hand to check each person's entitlement.

Pension Credit opens the door to a lot more than a top-up to a pension. People who claim it could access free dental care, free or discounted eye tests and glasses, a council tax reduction and help to pay their rent.
It can also bring access to Winter Fuel Vouchers and the Warm Home Discount Scheme, and a free TV licence for anyone over 75.
The session runs from 9.30am to 12.30pm on 28 October at Ty Dewi Sant, Carmarthen Road, Fforestfach, Swansea SA5 8HN. There is no need to book. Residents can simply come along and speak to the team.

Labour councillors know that many older people miss out on money they are entitled to, often because the forms feel daunting or they do not realise they qualify. Face-to-face help in the community takes that worry away.
With household bills still high, making sure every pensioner in Swansea gets the support they are due is a practical way the Labour administration is helping people through the winter.
This drop-in shows Labour's priorities for Swansea: a council that goes out to its communities, puts money back in people's pockets and looks after those who need help most.

images.alt: An older woman presses a calculator while a man beside her reads a letter

articles.sourceTitle: Could you be entitled to Pension Credit?

articles.headline: Labour welcomes glowing Estyn report for Penyrheol Comprehensive
articles.summary: Swansea Labour and local councillors congratulate pupils and staff at Penyrheol Comprehensive on a hugely positive Estyn report praising its caring, inclusive school.
body: Swansea Labour is congratulating pupils and staff at Penyrheol Comprehensive School on a hugely positive Estyn inspection report.

Inspectors found the school provides a caring, inclusive and supportive environment where pupils feel valued and develop a strong sense of belonging, built on its core values of 'Respect, Aspire, Thrive and Belong'.

They praised the strong relationships between staff and pupils, the valuable emotional, social and wellbeing support staff provide, and the school's robust safeguarding arrangements. Teaching was found to be effective in many areas, with many pupils behaving well, engaging positively in lessons and persevering with their work.

A particular strength is the school's support for pupils with additional learning needs (ALN). Inspectors described its Specialist Teaching Facility and wider ALN provision as highly nurturing, inclusive and effective. They also praised the broad curriculum of academic and vocational opportunities, and the clear strategic vision set by headteacher Damian Benney and the senior leadership team.
Labour's Cabinet Member for Education, Cllr Robert Smith, said: "Congratulations to everyone at Penyrheol Comprehensive School on this positive report."

Local Labour councillor for Gorseinon and Penyrheol, Cllr Andrew Stevens, said: "This is a fantastic report and a real credit to the pupils, staff and governors at Penyrheol. To see inspectors recognise the school's caring, inclusive ethos and its excellent support for pupils with additional learning needs makes us all very proud."

Fellow Labour ward councillor Cllr Jan Curtice said: "Penyrheol Comprehensive is at the heart of our community, and this report shows what a difference a school makes when every young person feels they belong. Well done to everyone involved."

Labour ward councillor Cllr Nicola Matthews added: "Congratulations to Mr Benney and the whole school team. We'll keep working with the school and local families to build on this success, so that every pupil has the chance to thrive."
Mr Benney said: "We are delighted that the report recognises the hard work, commitment and care shown every day by our staff, pupils, governors and wider school community."
Every child in Swansea deserves a school where they feel they belong and can thrive. Swansea Labour will keep backing Penyrheol and every school in the city to deliver just that.

images.alt: Penyrheol Comprehensive pupils holding Estyn certificates in the school hall with a member of staff

articles.sourceTitle: Penyrheol Comprehensive School praised in positive Estyn report

articles.headline: Labour takes forward plans for modern new learning spaces at Gowerton School
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council is taking forward plans, costing in excess of £47m, to give Gowerton School pupils modern new classrooms and improved facilities.
body: Swansea's Labour council is taking forward plans to give Gowerton School pupils modern new classrooms and improved facilities.
The total project cost is anticipated to be in excess of £47m and will be jointly funded with the Welsh Government under the Sustainable Communities for Learning programme.

The project will replace older parts of the school and temporary buildings with new, high-quality facilities. That means a more accessible site and classrooms, improved specialist spaces, and new buildings that are more energy efficient, supporting the council's commitment to tackling climate change. Families and the wider community will also have more opportunities to use school facilities outside the school day.

Under the revised design plans going before the Labour cabinet, some of the older buildings will need to be demolished, but historic elements will be kept wherever possible. Surveys showed that even with significant investment, some older buildings could not provide the modern, accessible learning environment that current and future pupils need.

School leaders, governors, staff and learners have all helped shape the project, and the school's senior leadership team and governing body have expressed their support for the revised plans. Once designs are finalised, the project will need further approval from cabinet and the Welsh Government.

Labour's Cabinet Member for Education and Learning, Cllr Robert Smith, said: "Our priority is to give young people in Gowerton the best possible place to learn. This investment will provide modern classrooms and facilities that support pupils every day, helping them to feel confident, comfortable and inspired to reach their full potential."
He added: "This project will make sure the school is ready to support pupils for many years to come."
Modern schools, ready for the future: Swansea Labour is investing in the next generation in Gowerton and across the city.

images.alt: Pupils in white school shirts writing with pencils at a classroom desk

articles.sourceTitle: Investment set to give Gowerton School pupils modern new learning spaces

articles.headline: Swansea Labour urges families to apply as free school meals reach Years 7 and 8
articles.summary: Families with children in Years 7 and 8 who receive Universal Credit can now apply for free school meals. Swansea's Labour council is urging every eligible family to apply.
body: More Swansea families can now get free school meals for their children, and Swansea's Labour council is urging every eligible family to apply.

Families with children in Years 7 and 8 whose parent, carer or guardian receives Universal Credit, regardless of earnings, can apply for the new Extended Free School Meals scheme, available from October 12. Eligible pupils receive a daily meal allowance of £2.40.

The move, funded by the Welsh Government, builds on the success of the Universal Primary Free School Meals programme, which already provides free school meals to all primary-aged pupils across Swansea and Wales. More than 18,000 primary school pupils in Swansea benefit from that offer.

Labour's Cabinet Member for Education, Cllr Robert Smith, said: "This expansion will help ensure more young people can benefit from a healthy meal during the school day. We know many households continue to face financial pressures, so extending free school meals to Year 7 and Year 8 pupils whose families receive Universal Credit will provide valuable support at a time when it is needed most."
He added: "We want to make sure every eligible family benefits from this new entitlement, so I would encourage parents and carers to submit an application as soon as possible."

The extended offer covers the food element of free school meals only. Eligibility for the Schools Essentials Grant stays subject to the existing criteria. Families can apply online through the free school meals page on the Swansea Council website.
No child should go hungry at school. Swansea Labour wants every family who is entitled to this help to get it.

images.alt: Secondary school pupils in white shirts smiling and looking at a phone in a library

articles.sourceTitle: Free meals offer extended to more Swansea secondary school pupils

articles.headline: Labour council repairs more Swansea roads, with Cockett next
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council has completed road repairs on Mynydd Newydd Road in Mynydd-bach, and highway teams are heading to the Cockett ward next.
body: Swansea's Labour council is pressing on with road repairs across the city, with more work done and more on the way.
Highway teams have recently been working in Mynydd-bach and have just completed a section of road on Mynydd Newydd Road.
Over the coming weeks, highway maintenance teams will visit the Cockett ward to carry out similar repairs, making sure roads are safe for motorists.
The council has thanked motorists for their patience while repairs continue. Details of planned maintenance schemes are on the council's Roadwatch page at swansea.gov.uk/roadwatch.
Safe, well-maintained roads matter to everyone. Swansea Labour is getting on with fixing them, street by street.

images.alt: Two highway workers in hi-vis clothing and helmets raking fresh tarmac into a road repair

articles.headline: Labour council's award-winning Christmas Parade returns on 22 November
articles.summary: Swansea's award-winning Christmas Parade returns on Sunday 22 November, with floats, performers, Santa, the Christmas lights switch-on and fireworks, put on by the Labour council.
body: Swansea's award-winning Christmas Parade returns on Sunday 22 November, as the city's Labour council brings Wales's biggest festive celebration back to the city centre.

Families can line the streets from 5pm to see community groups, festive floats, performers, much-loved characters and, of course, Santa himself. More than 40 local organisations, schools and community groups will take part.

The parade starts at the Guildhall, where Santa will open proceedings with a festive lighting display and fireworks. It then travels along St Helen's Road, through The Kingsway, across College Street, along Castle Street and Caer Street, before finishing on Princess Way.

Live entertainment will run on two stages, at the Guildhall and outside the Dragon Hotel, before Santa switches on Swansea's Christmas lights. The evening ends with a spectacular fireworks display. Last year the parade won Event of the Year (Local Authority) at the National Outdoor Events Association (NOEA) Awards.

Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: "The award-winning Swansea Christmas Parade is one of the highlights of the year and a fantastic opportunity for communities, residents and visitors to come together and celebrate the start of the festive season."

He added: "Alongside returning favourites, we're especially excited to unveil a brand-new parade float this year, which we think families are going to love. We'll keep the details under wraps for now, but anyone who's ever dreamed of reaching infinity and beyond should make sure they don't miss it."

Visitors can make a day of it with Swansea Winter Wonderland, complete with its ice rink and alpine-themed bar, and the Christmas Market. Swansea's Labour council is also running free buses that weekend, so families can get there more easily.
Bringing communities together and backing city centre businesses at Christmas: that's Swansea Labour delivering for the city.

images.alt: Santa and Mrs Claus waving from a lit-up sleigh float in falling snow at night

articles.sourceTitle: Swansea Christmas parade set to light up the city this festive season

articles.headline: Labour council shuts three more illegal vape shops in Swansea
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council has closed three more vape shops caught selling illegal vapes and counterfeit tobacco, two on St Helen's Road and one on Dilwyn Street.
body: Swansea's Labour council has shut three more vape shops that were selling illegal vapes and counterfeit tobacco, protecting residents and children from dangerous goods.
The shops are Vape City and Asia Vapes, both on St Helen's Road, and Vape Zone on Dilwyn Street. Swansea Magistrates enforced all three closures.

The closures were secured by the council's Trading Standards team working with the police. They are the latest step in the Labour administration's continued clampdown on counterfeit tobacco and illegal vapes across Swansea.

Labour's Cabinet Member for Development, Cllr Andrew Williams, said: "The latest closures are another great example of the work our Trading Standards is doing to disrupt and close down businesses that are operating illegally.
"It's completely unacceptable for many of these vape shops to operate in the way they are, selling counterfeit goods, particularly to children."

This is not a one-off. In June 2026, two vape shops in Pontarddulais and the city centre were closed after being caught selling illegal vapes. More recently, three vape shops on Mansel Street in the city centre were closed for three months, and two more were closed in Morriston.
Every closure takes illegal products off our high streets and sends a clear message to traders who break the law that Labour's council will act.
Keeping children safe and standing up for honest local businesses are priorities for Swansea Labour, and this latest action shows the council delivering on them.

images.alt: Asia Vape shop with its red roller shutter down and closure notices posted on it
Vape Zone shop front with closure notices posted in the window
Vape City shop front with closure notices posted in the window and on the door

articles.sourceTitle: Clampdown on illegal vape sellers in Swansea continues

articles.headline: Labour brings Wales' only dockless e-bike scheme to Swansea
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council has appointed Voi to run a city-wide e-bike scheme, the only dockless one in Wales, with free first rides and discounts for people on low incomes.
body: Swansea's Labour council is bringing Wales' only dockless e-bike scheme to the city, giving residents an affordable, sustainable new way to make short journeys.

The council has appointed Voi to run the 24-hour, city-wide service, which launches in the week of 26 October. It starts with 70 e-bikes across Swansea University campuses, the city centre and key transport hubs, and the fleet will grow in stages to 500 e-bikes within the first year.

Labour's Cabinet Member for Environment and Infrastructure, Cllr Andrew Stevens, said: "It has long been our ambition to have a Swansea-wide e-bike scheme and I'm delighted that we are partnering with Voi. Similar schemes around the UK have quickly become very well used, offering a new form of public transport and providing a convenient and sustainable travel option for everyday short journeys. Swansea will be the only place in Wales with a dockless e-bike scheme, and I'd encourage everyone to give it a go."

Keeping it affordable was central to Labour's choice of operator. Prices start at 50p to unlock an e-bike and 20p per minute, but the unlock fee is waived for the first six months and every new customer gets their first three 15-minute rides free. Day, week and monthly passes are available, with discounts for people on low incomes, NHS workers, people aged over 60, disabled people, military personnel and students.

Labour's Cabinet Member for Community, Cllr Rebecca Fogarty, said: "Key to our decision to partner with Voi was the affordable nature of the scheme. There are day, week and monthly passes available for regular users and a range of discounts available to many people including those on low incomes, making it a cost-effective way to travel around Swansea."

The scheme will connect Swansea's universities, city centre, transport hubs and communities, with an early focus on destinations such as Singleton Park and SA1. It is designed to work alongside new infrastructure including the Swansea Bay Metro and the Strand hub.

The e-bikes will be powered by 100% renewable energy and supported by a zero-emission operations fleet. The scheme will also create 18 jobs, as well as apprenticeships in sustainable transport operations.
Cheaper, greener journeys and new local jobs: this is Labour delivering a better-connected Swansea that works for everyone.

images.alt: Cllr Andrew Stevens and Cllr Rebecca Fogarty in helmets on orange Voi e-bikes outside a glass-fronted building

articles.sourceTitle: Swansea set for Wales' only dockless e-bike scheme

articles.headline: Labour council warns residents about Council Tax scam messages
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council is warning residents about scam emails claiming a credit has been added to their Council Tax account, and explains how to spot a genuine message.
body: Swansea's Labour council is urging residents to stop and think before clicking on Council Tax messages, after reports of scam emails doing the rounds.
The scam emails claim that a credit has been added to the recipient's Council Tax account and ask them to click a link to view the account or claim money back.
The council's advice is simple. Don't click suspicious links, don't provide personal or banking details, and don't use contact details contained in a suspicious message.

Swansea Council does send genuine emails and text messages about Council Tax, so it helps to know what to look for. Genuine Council Tax texts show as coming from Swansea.gov, and links in those texts start with ctaxsms.swansea.gov.uk. Genuine emails come from an address ending in swansea.gov.uk.
Anyone unsure whether a message is genuine should not take the risk. Residents can log on to their Swansea account and check their Council Tax balance online instead.

Labour councillors know how much damage a scam can do to a household budget, especially when money is tight. Getting clear warnings out quickly is part of how the Labour administration looks after the people it serves.

images.alt: A red and white 'Scam alert' graphic

articles.sourceName: Facebook posts by Cllr Rob Stewart and Swansea Council

articles.headline: Labour's £800,000 winter support package returns to help Swansea families
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council brings back Here For You This Winter with more than £800,000 for holiday hunger support, free buses, Christmas help and more. Community grant applications close 9 November.
body: Swansea's Labour council is putting more than £800,000 into supporting residents, families and communities this winter, as its Here For You This Winter campaign returns.

The package includes holiday hunger support to help feed school-aged children during the Christmas and February half-term holidays, extra support for foodbanks and community cafés, and funding for Swansea Spaces and community hubs helping families, children and people facing poverty or isolation.

Households struggling with festive costs can get direct help through the Councillor Voucher Scheme. Free bus travel returns on selected dates before and after Christmas, helping families get out and about while supporting local businesses.

The council is working with the charity Mr X to make sure children at risk of going without do not miss out on a Christmas gift. Together at Christmas returns to the Brangwyn Hall with a two-course meal, entertainment, clothing and support for people at risk of homelessness or isolation. Support for Multibank Cymru continues, helping people access clothing, household items and other necessities.

Last winter the campaign delivered around 30,000 meals to tackle holiday hunger, Christmas presents for 1,200 children who might otherwise have gone without, more than 130,000 free bus journeys, and direct support for hundreds of households facing financial hardship.

Community groups, charities and voluntary organisations can now apply for funding to help deliver support this winter. The deadline is 9 November, and applications are made at www.swansea.gov.uk/winterwellbeinggrant.
This is Labour's priorities in action: using the council's resources so that no family in Swansea faces winter alone, and backing the community groups who know their neighbourhoods best.

images.alt: A collage of a child eating pasta, a child opening a present, two older women having tea and a mother with her son

articles.sourceTitle: Winter can be a challenging time for many, but help is at hand.

articles.headline: Labour council backs greener future for The Bunkhouse music venue
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council has helped secure funding for green roofs, solar panels and roof repairs at The Bunkhouse, helping safeguard the much-loved city centre music venue.
body: Swansea's Labour council has helped secure funding to make The Bunkhouse, one of the city centre's much-loved music venues, more sustainable and resilient.
The improvements include green roofs, solar panels and roof repairs.
Working with partners, the council says it is helping safeguard the venue's future while supporting the city's cultural scene.
Grassroots venues like The Bunkhouse give local bands a stage and bring people into the city centre in the evening.
Supporting them is part of the Labour administration's wider work to keep Swansea city centre lively and welcoming.
This shows Labour's priorities for Swansea: backing the city's culture and its independent businesses while making the city centre greener.

images.alt: The Bunkhouse bar and music venue on a Swansea street, with tables and chairs outside

articles.sourceTitle: A greener future is taking shape at The Bunkhouse!

articles.headline: Labour welcomes milestone as Swansea cable car base station rises in Landore
articles.summary: Steel is going up at the base station for the new cable car to Kilvey Hill. Labour council leader Cllr Rob Stewart calls it another welcome milestone and a major investment in Swansea's future.
body: Swansea's Labour council has welcomed a new milestone in the city's cable car project, as the steel superstructure of the base station starts to go up at Landore.
The foundations of the base station, where guests will board the gondola for the journey up to Kilvey Hill, are now complete. Over the next few months the building will begin to take shape.
Labour's Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: “This is another welcome milestone in the development of Skyline’s exciting plans for Swansea.
“It’s great to see work progressing at Landore, with the foundations now complete and the next phase set to bring the gondola terminal building to life.
“This is a major investment in Swansea’s future, helping to strengthen our tourism offer, create new opportunities and further establish the city as a fantastic place to live, work and visit.
“We look forward to seeing further progress on this ambitious project over the coming months.”
The council says there is plenty more to come as the project moves forward.
The project shows Labour's ambition for Swansea: backing investment that brings in visitors, creates new opportunities and gives the city something to be proud of.

images.alt: A crane lifts steelwork onto a concrete column at a construction site, with a wooded hill behind

articles.sourceName: Facebook posts by Cllr Rob Stewart and Swansea Council
articles.sourceTitle: The base station is taking shape!

articles.headline: Labour's free Christmas buses return for a sixth year
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council is bringing back free bus travel for the Christmas Parade weekend and every festive weekend, helping families save on travel and backing city centre businesses.
body: Families across Swansea can travel free by bus again this Christmas, as Swansea's Labour council brings back its popular free festive bus offer for the sixth year running.

The free buses start on the Christmas Parade weekend, Saturday 21 and Sunday 22 November, when tens of thousands of people are expected in the city centre. They then run every weekend in the countdown to Christmas, and from 21 December to New Year's Eve.

The free bus dates are: 21 and 22 November; 28 and 29 November; 5 and 6 December; 12 and 13 December; 19 and 20 December; and 21 to 31 December, when buses are operating. As in previous years, only journeys that start and finish in Swansea are covered.

Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: "Swansea is the only council in Wales to offer this opportunity to take the bus and save money in the countdown to Christmas. It's the sixth year in a row that families have been able to take advantage of the offer. When we ran it last year, more than 131,000 journeys were completed, which just shows how important the service is."

He added: "Offering free buses to get to and from the Christmas parade is a brilliant early festive present for local families on what will be a great curtain-raiser for the countdown. We know that people also travel from across South and West Wales for this event and it's an important boost to city centre shops, cafes and other businesses at a vital time of year for them."

Labour's Cabinet Member for Community Support, Cllr Rebecca Fogarty, said the free buses are part of the Labour council's wider winter support: "This offer will be part of a comprehensive package of support for those most in need. We're working on initiatives that will include food support, activities, events and welcoming spaces to help residents this winter. Christmas can be an expensive time for everyone and a single family trip on free bus weekends can save them up to £20 in travel costs."

She added: "This offer is not just about encouraging people into the city centre - although we do want businesses to benefit from seeing more people coming into the city. This is also about giving the public the chance to travel all across Swansea, whether it's to visit family members or just enjoy what Swansea has to offer."

Free festive buses are a practical way Swansea Labour helps families with the cost of living while bringing more shoppers to local businesses. Labour introduced the scheme and has kept it going year after year, because Labour is here for Swansea.

images.alt: Illuminated reindeer and a sleigh float with Father Christmas waving, under falling snow at night

articles.sourceTitle: Free bus rides return for Christmas
articles.sourceName: a Facebook post by Cllr Rob Stewart

articles.headline: Labour council gives officers new powers to tackle anti-social behaviour
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour cabinet has approved new powers for trained council officers to tackle anti-social behaviour and protect vulnerable residents, including from cuckooing.
body: Swansea's Labour council is giving trained officers new ways to tackle anti-social behaviour and keep communities safe, after the Labour cabinet approved new powers for Housing Services and City Centre Management staff.

Officers will be able to use Community Protection Warnings and Community Protection Notices where someone's behaviour is having an ongoing harmful effect on others. A Warning is the first formal step. If the behaviour continues, a Notice may be considered after an assessment of the evidence and circumstances. Failing to comply with a Notice is a criminal offence.

In serious cases, Housing officers will also be able to seek Closure Orders to protect residents from persistent nuisance, criminality or exploitation. That includes suspected cuckooing, where criminals exploit vulnerable people and take over their homes for criminal activity.

Labour's Deputy Leader and Cabinet Member for Transformation, Cllr Andrea Harrington, said: "Everyone deserves to feel safe in their home, neighbourhood and community. These proposals would provide Housing Services and City Centre Management with additional options to address anti-social behaviour in a proportionate and constructive way. We recognise the impact anti-social behaviour can have on residents and businesses, while also understanding that there can be underlying issues driving that behaviour. Our focus is on early intervention, support and positive action wherever possible, while ensuring appropriate measures are available to protect individuals and communities when needed."

The new powers sit alongside a three-year Public Spaces Protection Order approved in September covering the city centre, beachfront and Dyfatty. Under the previous order, more than 1,100 interventions were carried out over two years. More than 230 led to further police action and more than 80 resulted in referrals for support or safeguarding. The new order includes measures tackling alcohol-related nuisance, public disorder and the dangerous use of e-bikes, scooters and other mechanically propelled vehicles.

Labour's Deputy Leader and Cabinet Member for Investment and Delivery, Cllr David Hopkins, said: "We want Swansea's city centre, beachfront and residential communities to be welcoming, safe and enjoyable places for everyone. The review shows that the existing PSPO has made a positive difference, helping partners tackle anti-social behaviour, support vulnerable people and improve confidence in our public spaces."

He added: "The measures approved by Cabinet will ensure these powers remain available where they are needed, while maintaining the balanced and safeguarding-led approach that has been central to Swansea's scheme."

The work is part of the Safer Swansea Partnership, which brings together the council, South Wales Police and other organisations. The review of the order found support for continuing and strengthening it from partners including South Wales Police, businesses, Swansea BID and elected members.

Labour's approach is firm on the people causing harm and supportive of those who need help. It shows Swansea Labour's commitment to safer streets, safer homes and communities where everyone feels welcome.

images.alt: Rows of terraced houses on a hillside under a blue sky, with flowering shrubs in front

articles.sourceTitle: New measures to tackle anti-social behaviour (Swansea Council Facebook post)

articles.headline: Labour's Mansel Road resurfacing in Bonymaen restarts on Monday
articles.summary: Resurfacing of Mansel Road in Bonymaen, part of Labour's work on local roads, restarts on Monday 26 October after weather delays, with the remaining work done in the daytime.
body: Work to resurface Mansel Road in Bonymaen restarts on Monday 26 October, as Swansea's Labour council carries on fixing local roads.
The council's highways maintenance teams started the scheme in the week of 19 to 23 October, working overnight between 8pm and 5am, but ongoing poor weather has delayed the work.
When it restarts on Monday, the remaining work will be done in the daytime, between 9am and 5pm.
The road will be closed during the works so that the upgrade can be finished quickly and safely. Diversions will be in place.
Good roads matter to every resident, and Labour is getting on with the job. Once finished, the scheme means a better road for people who live on Mansel Road and everyone who travels through Bonymaen.

images.alt: Road resurfacing lorries working on a residential street at night under streetlights

articles.sourceName: Facebook posts by Cllr Rob Stewart and Swansea Council

articles.headline: Labour council's family Bonfire Night returns to Singleton Park
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council puts on its annual Bonfire Night at Singleton Park on 5 November, with fireworks, lasers and a fire show, and family tickets from £13 in advance.
body: Swansea's annual Bonfire Night fireworks display returns to Singleton Park on 5 November, as Swansea's Labour council puts on a safe, affordable night out for families.

The evening includes fireworks, laser effects, magical characters, live entertainment and a fire show before the main display. Gates open at 5pm, the fire show starts at 6.45pm and the main fireworks display begins at 7.30pm.

Tickets are cheaper in advance: adults £6 (£7 on the day), children and concessions £5 (£6 on the day), Passport to Leisure holders £4, a family of four £13 (£18 on the day) and a family of five £15 (£20 on the day).

Event parking is available at Singleton Lacrosse Field and Recreation Ground for £5 per vehicle, paid on the day. Food and drink vendors will be on site, so families can come early and make an evening of it.
Booking now saves money compared with on-the-day prices.
With the cost of living still squeezing family budgets, Swansea Labour is proud to see a safe, well-run Bonfire Night that families can afford, with low-cost tickets for Passport to Leisure holders.
